name: Hemi-myelomeningocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Myelomeningocele

criteria.description: Presence of a unilateral open neural tube defect with protrusion of meninges and spinal cord tissue
Evidence of spinal cord malformation and tethering on imaging studies
Unilateral lower limb motor and sensory deficits corresponding to the lesion level
Presence of cutaneous stigmata such as hemilateral skin dimples or tufts of hair overlying the defect

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of unilateral open spinal defect with protruding meninges and spinal cord tissue plus corresponding unilateral neurological deficits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by clinical examination and MRI imaging of the spine.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral spinal cord herniation with meningocele sac
searchTerms: spinal cord bulge with fluid sac on one side
one-sided spinal cord hernia with sac
loss of movement in one lower limb

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral sensory loss below lesion level
searchTerms: loss of feeling below spinal injury on one side

common.symptomName: Lower limb muscle atrophy on affected side
searchTerms: shrinkage of leg muscles on affected side
loss of muscle bulk in lower limb

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata such as hemilateral skin dimples or hair tufts
searchTerms: skin dimples or hair patches on one side
skin marks like dimples or hair tufts
unusual skin features on half the body

occasional.symptomName: Hydrocephalus due to associated Chiari II malformation
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from Chiari malformation
excess brain fluid due to Chiari II
difficulty with bowel movements due to nerves

occasional.symptomName: Lower limb spasticity on affected side

rare.symptomName: Seizures related to associated brain malformations
searchTerms: fits linked to brain structural issues

rare.symptomName: Cognitive impairment due to hydrocephalus complications
searchTerms: thinking problems from brain fluid buildup
memory and learning issues from brain swelling

rare.symptomName: Skin ulceration overlying the meningocele sac
searchTerms: ulcer on back skin above meningocele
open skin wound at spinal defect site

laboratory: Urinalysis may show signs of urinary tract infection secondary to neurogenic bladder
imaging: MRI demonstrating unilateral open spinal defect with herniation of meninges and spinal cord
Ultrasound or MRI showing associated hydrocephalus or Chiari II malformation
X-rays showing spinal deformities and orthopedic abnormalities
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; multifactorial etiology with environmental and genetic risk factors
other: Prenatal ultrasound may detect spinal defect
Fetal MRI can provide detailed anatomical assessment

distinguishingFeatures: Closed spinal defect without meningeal or spinal cord herniation
Usually asymptomatic or mild cutaneous signs

redFlags: Signs of infection or ulceration over meningocele sac
Development of hydrocephalus with increased intracranial pressure
references: Neurology Clinics. Myelomeningocele and related spinal dysraphisms. 2020.
